site.name: Evening Post Mine
site.location: Switzerland Park / Boulder County Tungsten Mining District
overview: Evening Post Mine was a documented tungsten property at Switzerland Park in Boulder County's historic tungsten district, with separate tunnel and shaft workings developed on a short northeast-striking vein.
Federal and Colorado mining records preserve unusually specific details about the mine's location, underground layout, production history, and geology.

timeline.text: The mine was developed by an adit and a shaft system on a short tungsten-bearing vein in granite. Recorded production came from the shaft workings rather than the tunnel.
USGS reporting states that Sewell and Bronson carried out limited work in the upper part of the shaft workings.
USGS Professional Paper 245 mapped the Evening Post workings, while Colorado's tungsten-mine inventory recorded an approximately 1,150-foot adit and a shaft with three levels.

moreHistory: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 245 places the Evening Post tunnel at about 7,560 feet elevation in the North Boulder Creek valley at Switzerland Park, 3,200 feet south 84 degrees east of Peewink Mountain. The shaft workings were about 1,000 feet south of the tunnel portal and roughly 400 feet higher.

Colorado's Tungsten Mines of Colorado records less than 10,000 tungsten units produced from the shaft and none from the adit. It describes the workings as an approximately 1,150-foot adit and a shaft with three levels on a short northeast-striking vein in granite.

The retained point near 40.00296, -105.42889 is an approximate historic tunnel-locality point derived from the USGS published distance and bearing from Peewink Mountain. It identifies the documented mine locality without claiming that a surviving opening has been field surveyed or is safe or publicly accessible.
